# Real UFW canonical byte references

These files contain only documentation/benchmark IP addresses and fixture comments. They were generated by the installed Ubuntu UFW CLI in fresh, network-isolated Docker containers with `NET_ADMIN` and `NET_RAW`. No production host, credential, nginx file or engine was used.

The generator is `ansible/molecule/cloudfront_sync/ufw_reference_verify.py`. It refuses a non-container environment or a missing/wrong root-only disposable marker before running UFW, and refuses to overwrite nonempty output. The marker is not a defense against a malicious root; it prevents accidental invocation on an ordinary host. The caller must also provide `--network none` and must never use the host network or mount host policy directories.

## Recorded provenance

| Directory | Ubuntu | UFW package |
|---|---|---|
| `22.04` | 22.04 | `0.36.1-4ubuntu0.1` |
| `24.04` | 24.04 | `0.36.2-6` |
| `26.04` | 26.04 | `0.36.2-9build1` |

Each manifest records the package version, source-function hashes, original CLI commands, ordered transition commands, file mode/owner/group, and SHA256 for every file. `_write_rules` and `UFWRule.format_rule` are identical across these three package builds. The 16 user-file byte sequences are also identical across all three OS references; this is an observed result for these fixtures, not a promise that arbitrary UFW versions or configurations have the same format.

## Cases

The before state contains unmanaged SSH LIMIT, an admin-source allow, deny, reject, log + multiport, routed in/out interfaces, an inbound interface, an application profile with spaces, an outbound interface, IPv6, and a trailing anchor. Existing owned IPv4/IPv6 CloudFront-shaped tuples use comment `cloudfront-sync`.

Seven actual CLI transitions produce eight states:

1. `before`: active real UFW and initial rules.
2. `after_add4`: append an owned IPv4 tuple.
3. `after_add6`: append an owned IPv6 tuple.
4. `after_delete4`: remove the old owned IPv4 tuple.
5. `after_restore4`: insert it at its original family position, before the surviving unmanaged anchor.
6. `after_delete6`: remove the added IPv6 tuple.
7. `after_rollback`: remove the added IPv4 tuple; both full user files match `before` exactly.
8. `after_noop`: re-add an existing identical tuple; both full user files still match `before` exactly.

After each operation, the generator verifies that every other UFW configuration file retains its path, bytes, mode, uid and gid. There are 11 such protected files in this fixture image (the fixture app contributes one); this is not a hardcoded production inventory count.

The ordered transition references above use low logging and default-deny incoming/default-allow outgoing/default-deny routed.

The additional `profiles/{22.04,24.04,26.04}/` matrix covers nine configurations per OS: off/low/medium/high/full logging, mixed allow/deny/reject policies, all-allow policies, all-reject policies, and off logging with all-allow policies. Each configuration includes any protocol with and without a port, TCP reject, log-all, logged LIMIT, simultaneous source/destination multiport, IPv4 /32 and IPv6 /128 hosts, a multi-protocol/multiport application, and generic SSH LIMIT. All 18 file byte sequences are identical across the three OS matrix references. Each matrix manifest records the exact profiles and CLI commands.

All these live references have the stock limit capability enabled. Other capability or package profiles must have their own explicit evidence or be refused before mutation. These samples must not be treated as permission to ignore unknown lines, noncanonical blocks, unsupported profiles, or any residual bytes.

## Reproduce without overwriting checked-in evidence

Use a fresh empty output directory, substitute the chosen version, and mount only this repository read-only plus that output directory read-write. For example:

```sh
# Set reviewed absolute paths; never mount host /etc or use --network host.
# The Python bootstrap creates only the disposable container marker.
docker run --rm --network none --cap-add NET_ADMIN --cap-add NET_RAW \
  --entrypoint /usr/bin/python3 \
  -v /absolute/path/to/repository:/work:ro \
  -v /absolute/path/to/empty/output:/out \
  cloudfront-sync-validation:26.04 \
  -c 'import os,sys,runpy; p="/run/cloudfront-sync-ufw-reference-fixture"; f=os.open(p,os.O_CREAT|os.O_EXCL|os.O_WRONLY,0o600); os.write(f,b"CloudFront pure UFW reference fixture only\n"); os.close(f); sys.argv=["ufw_reference_verify.py","--output","/out"]; runpy.run_path("/work/ansible/molecule/cloudfront_sync/ufw_reference_verify.py",run_name="__main__")'
```

Compare every generated `.rules` file and its manifest hash with this directory. The generator itself must never be invoked against production or imported into the runtime adapter/guardian. UFW capability probing mutates temporary kernel chains; this harness performs it only inside the explicitly isolated fixture container.

Append `--matrix` to the generator arguments to reproduce the additional profile matrix in a separate empty output directory. Append `--adapter /work/ansible/roles/cloudfront_sync/files/ufw_integrity.py` to calibrate the pure parser and predictor against actual UFW output. With an adapter, the harness compiles an exact in-memory copy of its bytes, records their SHA256, and refuses a source change during the run. The normal suite verifies 16 full round-trips, six add/delete/insert transitions, six unchanged-family checks, and one actual UFW no-op; the matrix verifies 18 full round-trips.
